# Autoware overhead analysis — campaign `overhead_aw_20260906_163330` (2026-09-06)

**Setup.** Autoware logging simulator + sample rosbag at rate 0.5, image `autoware-dev-trt-a1000-fishwait10`.
Modes: baseline (no FISH), LTTng (FISH tracepoints, 42-event whitelist, `rmw_take` filtered to `taken == 1`),
LTTng+nsys (same + CUPTI via the lean nsys profile: `--trace=cuda --sample=none --cpuctxsw=none --cuda-event-trace=false`).
3 repetitions per mode. CPU placement "split": application + nsys on the 6 P-cores (0,2,4,6,8,10), observer
(LTTng daemons, FISH daemon, probes) on E-cores 12–17, host desktop on 18–19; SMT off, turbo off, performance governor.
`lo` multicast ON (Cyclone DDS single-host). Every traced run: trace 212–213 MB, 0 discarded events, stop 171–192 s after replay end.

**Phases** (from diagnostic header stamps, sim time): (1) first non-zero diag stamp, (2) first report of the tracker in
`pipeline_latency_monitor` (= NDT active, all perception stages running), (3) last advancing stamp (bag end).
Warm-up = (1)→(2), execution = (2)→(3). All values below are execution-phase unless stated. Values are sim time
(rate 0.5 → wall time is 2×); ratios are unaffected.

| run | warm-up (1)→(2) [s] | execution (2)→(3) [s] |
|---|---|---|
| baseline 1 / 2 / 3 | 4.6 / 6.4 / 4.8 | 25.3 / 23.5 / 25.1 |
| LTTng 1 / 2 / 3 | 5.8 / 7.1 / 6.8 | 24.1 / 22.8 / 23.1 |
| LTTng+nsys 1 / 2 / 3 | 6.4 / 8.1 / 7.0 | 23.4 / 21.8 / 22.9 |

## 1. Total Latency (`autoware_pipeline_latency_monitor`)

Definition (param yaml in the image): time-ordered chain of the latest per-step latencies, steps
`multi_object_tracker` (`debug/meas_to_tracked_object_ms`) → `decorative_object_merger_node` → `map_based_prediction`
(`processing_time_ms`) → `planning` → `control`, plus constant offsets sensing 0 + perception 1.4 + planning 50 +
control 15 + vehicle interface 191 = **257.4 ms**. In a goal-less replay `decorative_object_merger_node`, `planning`
and `control` never report (listed in `uninitialized_inputs` in every run), so the measured part ("chain") is
tracker step + prediction step: **chain = Total − 257.4 ms**.

| mode | run 1 | run 2 | run 3 | mean ± sd [ms] | Δ | chain [ms] | chain Δ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| baseline | 403.1 | 409.3 | 410.8 | 407.7 ± 3.3 | — | 150.3 | — |
| LTTng | 439.2 | 433.8 | 455.5 | 442.8 ± 9.2 | +8.6 % | 185.4 | +23.3 % |
| LTTng+nsys (lean) | 441.3 | 449.2 | 427.1 | 439.2 ± 9.1 | +7.7 % | 181.8 | +21.0 % |

Reference, previous day (`overhead_aw_20260905_split`, same placement, old nsys profile with CPU sampling and
context-switch tracing on, `lo` multicast OFF): baseline 404.6 ± 5.9, LTTng 446.4 ± 7.0 (+10.3 %), LTTng+nsys
451.4 ± 6.2 (+11.6 %); chain 147.2 → 189.0 (+28.4 %) → 194.0 (+31.8 %).

## 7. Reading

- The lean nsys profile adds nothing measurable on top of LTTng in Autoware: identical DDS and executor delays,
  +1–3 % callback execution (+11 % on timers), Total Latency difference within one standard deviation. With the previous
  profile (CPU sampling + context-switch tracing on by default) nsys was +1.3 points above LTTng.
- LTTng costs +9 % Total Latency, +23 % on the measured chain; the whole increase sits in the tracker step
  (+35 ms). Up to the concatenated cloud the pipeline latency grows by +10 ms (sensing filters +1/+1/+2, concat +10);
  the remaining ~+20 ms arises between the concatenated cloud and the tracked objects. Callback growth measured by the
  nodes' own diagnostics explains ~7 ms; DDS hops (0.3–2.7 ms each) and executor dispatch (µs) cannot. The tracker's
  extrapolation time doubling (14 → 28 ms) shows its input arriving later relative to its publish timer.
- `lo` multicast: the previous day's traces (multicast off) show 2–3× larger DDS hop latencies on the same topics;
  all campaigns before 2026-09-06 carry that inflation in hop metrics (not in Total Latency, which is dominated by the
  pipeline's own periods).
- Open: locating the remaining +20 ms needs baseline timing of the validator/merger/tracker stages — their own
  `debug/processing_time_ms` and `pipeline_latency_ms` topics are published in every mode and can be recorded by the
  diag probe; per-process CPU accounting is needed to explain the +1.85 app-set cores under LTTng (2.58 → 4.43).
